\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাওয়া} (bheste jāoyā)}{ভেস্তে যাওয়া (bheste jāoyā)}]{\bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাওয়া} (bheste jāoyā) — to fall through; to come to nothing}

\label{lesson:BN-C542-bheste-jaoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a queue token, then the Bengali for a phase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাওয়া}} — \emph{bheste jāoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fall through; to come to nothing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বৃষ্টি} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{বেড়ানোর} \bn{পরিকল্পনা} \bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Brishṭi hôle āmāder beṛānor pôrikôlpônā bheste jābe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, our plan for an outing will fall through.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{পরিকল্পনা} \bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{গেল}, \emph{sei pôrikôlpônā bheste gelô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভেস্তে} \bn{যাওয়া}} (\emph{bheste jāoyā}) joins \bn{ভেস্তে}, a word heard only in this phrase, to \bn{যাওয়া}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}; where \bn{ভেস্তে} comes from is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bheste jāoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bheste jāoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Brishṭi hôle āmāder beṛānor pôrikôlpônā bheste jābe.} — If it rains, our plan for an outing will fall through.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a queue token, then the Bengali for a phase, then say \emph{bheste jāoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নিষ্ফল} (nishphôl)}{নিষ্ফল (nishphôl)}]{\bn{নিষ্ফল} (nishphôl) — fruitless; in vain}

\label{lesson:BN-C542-nishphol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a phase, then the Bengali for to fall through.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নিষ্ফল}}
\textbf{\bn{নিষ্ফল}} — \emph{nishphôl} — \textquotedblleft{}fruitless; in vain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমাদের} \bn{সব} \bn{পরিকল্পনা} \bn{নিষ্ফল} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Āmāder sôb pôrikôlpônā nishphôl hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
All our plans came to nothing.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নিষ্ফল}} (\emph{nishphôl}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{niṣphala}, \textquotedblleft{}bearing no fruit, useless\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Āmāder sôb pôrikôlpônā nishphôl hôlô.} — All our plans came to nothing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a phase, then the Bengali for to fall through, then say \emph{nishphôl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিশৃঙ্খল} (bishringkhôl)}{বিশৃঙ্খল (bishringkhôl)}]{\bn{বিশৃঙ্খল} (bishringkhôl) — disorderly; in chaos}

\label{lesson:BN-C542-bishringkhol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to fall through, then the Bengali for fruitless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিশৃঙ্খল}}
\textbf{\bn{বিশৃঙ্খল}} — \emph{bishringkhôl} — \textquotedblleft{}disorderly; in chaos\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\textbf{\bn{বিশৃঙ্খল}} (\emph{bishringkhôl}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{viśṛṅkhala}, \textquotedblleft{}unfettered\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{śṛṅkhala}, \textquotedblleft{}a chain\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): with nothing holding it in order.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{খসা} (khôsā)}{খসা (khôsā)}]{\bn{খসা} (khôsā) — to come loose; to fall off}

\label{lesson:BN-C542-khosa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for fruitless, then the Bengali for in chaos.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{খসা}}
\textbf{\bn{খসা}} — \emph{khôsā} — \textquotedblleft{}to come loose; to fall off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জামার} \bn{একটা} \bn{বোতাম} \bn{খসল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jāmār ekṭā botām khôslô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A button came off my shirt.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{ইট} \bn{খসল}, \emph{sei iṭ khôslô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{খসা}} (\emph{khôsā}) comes from a reconstructed \emph{khasati}, \textquotedblleft{}slips\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{khasā}, \textquotedblleft{}to fall off, to slip away\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3856).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গোলমাল} (golmāl)}{গোলমাল (golmāl)}]{\bn{গোলমাল} (golmāl) — a muddle; trouble}

\label{lesson:BN-C542-golmal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for in chaos, then the Bengali for to come loose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গোলমাল}}
\textbf{\bn{গোলমাল}} — \emph{golmāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a muddle; trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{টিকিটে} \bn{নামের} \bn{গোলমাল} \bn{ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ṭikiṭe nāmer golmāl chhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a mix-up with the name on the ticket.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গোলমাল}} (\emph{golmāl}) is an expressive word for noise, trouble or a mix-up; its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.
